A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentOCR work. The main text, equations, five tables, nine figures, two algorithms, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original ALFWorld and search-based QA experiments, compression measurements, and cache and self-compression ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results and efficiency and ablation experiments in Section 5, alongside the appendix case study.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same optical-memory encoding, segment caching, compression decisions, success-conditioned reward, and intermittent reward schedule.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six ALFWorld task categories and seven QA datasets: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, and Bamboogle. No evaluation domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain Text (w/o RL), OCR (w/o RL), and Text + GRPO. Table 3 retains No Cache and Naive Cache. The newly cited HGPO does not participate in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same model sizes, prompt and response limits, interaction horizons, retrieval procedure, sampling and decoding settings, and 150 training iterations. Evaluation metrics remain success rate, exact match, and the same efficiency measurements.

E4.justification: The compression-factor sweep in Figure 3, cache ablation in Table 3, self-compression and reward-schedule ablations in Table 4, and HotpotQA case study in Appendix C are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark scores. Table 3 retains the same least-squares definition of growth over steps 1-50.

E6.justification: All matched result entries in Tables 1-4 and Figure 3 are unchanged, including AgentOCR's ALFWorld averages of 78.2% and 81.2%, QA averages of 34.2% and 40.1%, and 20.79-fold cache speedup. Appendix C retains the same trajectory and outputs.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8, the sequential decision-making formulation, GRPO objective, and cache-complexity arguments are mathematically unchanged. Differences in mathematical typography do not introduce new definitions, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about optical history, segment caching, adaptive self-compression, performance retention, and token savings. Abstract shortening does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The new Ethical Considerations section explicitly notes the absence of real-world deployment and interprets token savings as potentially supporting energy-efficient AI and resource-constrained devices. Existing result interpretations and the three technical limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B retain the same pseudocode, training hyperparameters, H100 configurations, rendering settings, and prompt templates. The existing code link moves into the abstract without changing the stated access information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds HGPO and its reference, He et al. (2026), Hierarchy-of-groups policy optimization for long-horizon agentic tasks. The remaining research positioning is retained; bibliography style and author-list formatting changes do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: v3 lightly shortens the abstract, revises author/contact presentation, makes Limitations unnumbered, and adds Ethical Considerations and Acknowledgments, including writing-assistance and funding disclosures. The existing narrative and appendix prose remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the predominantly single-column design and colored title/header styling with a two-column format. Figures, tables, algorithms, and appendix prompt panels are extensively resized and repositioned, including Figure 3 and Tables 3-4, while retaining their scientific content.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and technical limitations. The added citation and ethics, writing-assistance, and funding disclosures provide limited context, while the extensive layout conversion does not materially strengthen or weaken the paper's scientific support or overall quality.
